words.definition: the study of living things
words.example: In {biology}, we study how plants grow from seeds.

words.definition: the study of substances and how they change
words.example: In {chemistry}, we test how two liquids react together.

words.definition: the study of forces, light, heat and movement
words.example: Our {physics} project measures how gravity changes a falling ball's speed.

words.definition: books, poems and plays studied as writing
words.example: Our {literature} course compares poems and plays from different centuries.

words.definition: a room where people do scientific tests
words.example: We wear safety glasses in the science {laboratory}.

words.definition: a small machine that works out numbers
words.example: This pocket {calculator} has number keys and a screen for displaying sums.

words.definition: a group of sentences about one main idea
words.example: Indent the first line of each {paragraph}, a group of sentences.

words.definition: one of the main numbered parts of a book
words.example: This novel's fifth {chapter} begins on page sixty and ends on page seventy.

words.definition: the way someone forms letters with a pen
words.example: Your {handwriting} is easier to read when you form each letter clearly.

words.definition: studying again to prepare for a test
words.example: My exam {revision} includes rereading notes and testing myself.

words.definition: to study something again before a test
words.example: Before exams, I {revise} by studying the topics I have already learnt.

words.definition: to draw a line below written words
words.example: Please {underline} the title by drawing a line below it.

words.definition: to make the sounds of a word
words.example: How do you {pronounce} this word: does it rhyme with chair?

words.definition: to change words from one language into another
words.example: Can you {translate} this French sentence into English?

words.definition: to learn something so you can say it without looking
words.example: Actors {memorise} their lines, learning every word by heart before performing.

words.definition: to give all your attention to one thing
words.example: I cannot {concentrate} on my work with three conversations around me.

words.definition: to become better or make something better
words.example: Daily practice will {improve} my spelling until I make fewer mistakes.

words.definition: to look at something to find out whether it is correct
words.example: Before handing work in, I {check} each answer for mistakes.

words.definition: to find the answer to a problem
words.example: To {solve} a puzzle means to find its correct answer.

words.definition: to talk about something and share ideas
words.example: We {discuss} our plans aloud, taking turns to give our opinions.

words.definition: a set of pages that you can visit on the internet
words.example: The museum's {website} has online pages about opening times and exhibitions.

words.definition: a program used to open pages on the internet
words.example: I type the web address into my {browser} to open the page.

words.definition: to copy a file from the internet onto your device
words.example: I {download} the worksheet from the internet onto my tablet before going offline.

words.definition: to send a file from your device to the internet
words.example: We {upload} our video from the tablet to the school's website.

words.definition: to remove something stored on a device
words.example: I will {delete} the unwanted file so it no longer exists.

words.definition: to give something a different name
words.example: I {rename} the file from draft.txt to final.txt without changing its contents.

words.definition: to press a mouse button to choose something on screen
words.example: With the mouse, I {click} the arrow once to open the menu.

words.definition: a named set of information stored on a device
words.example: The photo is stored as a JPEG {file} called beach.jpg.

words.definition: a named place on a device that holds files
words.example: I keep all ten science files together in one {folder}.

words.definition: something on a web page that opens another page when chosen
words.example: This {link} is a clickable web address that takes you to another page.

words.definition: someone travelling in a vehicle without driving it
words.example: I travelled as a {passenger}, sitting beside my sister while she drove.

words.definition: the raised area beside railway tracks where people board trains
words.example: Our train leaves from {platform} six, beside the railway tracks.

words.definition: the act or time of leaving a place
words.example: The board lists our train's {departure} as ten o'clock, when it leaves.

words.definition: the place you are travelling to
words.example: The bus's final {destination} is York, where our journey ends.

words.definition: the price of a journey on public transport
words.example: The bus {fare} is two pounds for a single journey.

words.definition: the way taken to get from one place to another
words.example: The red line on this map shows our walking {route}.

words.definition: extra time spent waiting because something happens later than planned
words.example: A ten-minute {delay} means our train will leave later than planned.

words.definition: a travel pass for going somewhere and coming back
words.example: This {return ticket} is a travel pass for going there and coming back.

words.definition: bags and cases you take when travelling
words.example: The airline weighs all our {luggage}, including both suitcases.

words.definition: a strap that keeps you safely in your seat
words.example: Fasten your {seat belt} across your body before the car moves.

words.definition: a cheap place to stay, often with shared bedrooms
words.example: Our youth {hostel} has bunk beds shared by six travellers.

words.definition: the desk at a hotel where guests first give their details
words.example: Ask at hotel {reception} for your room key when you arrive.

words.definition: an arrangement to keep a room or seat for you
words.example: Our hotel {reservation} guarantees us a room for Friday night.

words.definition: a book with information for people visiting a place
words.example: I bought a printed {guidebook} full of tips for tourists visiting Rome.

words.definition: something you keep to remember a place you visited
words.example: I bought this little tower as a {souvenir} of our trip.

words.definition: the type of money used in a country
words.example: The pound is the {currency} used in the United Kingdom.

words.definition: in or to a different country
words.example: We travelled {abroad}, leaving Britain to spend a week in France.

words.definition: belonging to the area near you
words.example: Our {local} library is just two streets from our house.

words.definition: from a country other than your own
words.example: At the border, we exchanged pounds for {foreign} money from another country.

words.definition: full of people with little room to move
words.example: The bus was so {crowded} that nobody else could squeeze inside.

words.definition: a change in your body that shows you may be ill
words.example: A high temperature can be a {symptom} of an illness.

words.definition: a measure of how hot or cold something is
words.example: The thermometer shows my {temperature} is thirty-seven degrees.

words.definition: pain in the part inside your neck used for swallowing
words.example: Swallowing hurts because I have a {sore throat}.

words.definition: an agreed time to meet someone
words.example: My dental {appointment} is booked for three o'clock on Tuesday.

words.definition: a person receiving care from a doctor or nurse
words.example: The nurse calls the next {patient} into the doctor's room.

words.definition: a long strip of cloth wrapped around a hurt body part
words.example: The nurse wraps a {bandage} around my injured wrist.

words.definition: time spent relaxing instead of being active
words.example: After the long walk, I need some quiet {rest}, lying still without doing anything.

words.definition: to become well again after being ill or hurt
words.example: It took a week to {recover} from flu and feel well again.

words.definition: well and free from illness
words.example: The {healthy} seedlings have green leaves and strong roots, with no disease.

words.definition: strong enough to do physical activity without getting tired quickly
words.example: I am healthy but not {fit}; running leaves me tired within minutes.

words.definition: the natural world around us, including land, water and air
words.example: We study the {environment}: the natural world, including air, water and land.

words.definition: animals and plants that live freely in nature
words.example: Local {wildlife} consists of wild animals and plants, rather than pets or crops.

words.definition: small pieces of waste left lying in public places
words.example: Volunteers picked up {litter}, including wrappers dropped beside the path.

words.definition: the natural place where an animal or plant lives
words.example: Melting sea ice destroys the polar bear's {habitat}, its natural home.

words.definition: a long period with very little or no rain
words.example: After months without rain, the {drought} left fields dry and dusty.

words.definition: water covering land that is normally dry
words.example: The river overflowed, causing a {flood} in nearby streets.

words.definition: able to be used again instead of being thrown away
words.example: This {reusable} bottle is designed to be filled again hundreds of times.

words.definition: to make something smaller in amount or size
words.example: Please {reduce} this number from ten to five, making it smaller.

words.definition: to use more of something than you need
words.example: Please don't {waste} paper by printing fifty copies nobody needs.

words.definition: to put seeds or young trees into soil to grow
words.example: We will {plant} these seeds in soil and wait for shoots.

words.definition: a film or programme that gives facts about real life
words.example: The {documentary} is a factual film explaining real events, without fictional scenes or advertising.

words.definition: a film or programme made from moving drawings
words.example: The {cartoon} is a fictional film of moving drawings, without any advertising.

words.definition: the title of a news story
words.example: The newspaper's {headline} reads: Local School Wins Science Prize.

words.definition: a message intended to make people buy or use something
words.example: The thirty-second television {advert} ends by asking viewers to buy a sofa.

words.definition: a meeting where someone asks another person questions
words.example: The {interview} is a reporter's question-and-answer meeting with an author.

words.definition: the people watching or listening to a show
words.example: The {audience} clapped from their seats after the play ended.

words.definition: a person or creature in a story
words.example: My favourite {character} in this novel is the brave young detective.

words.definition: the main events in a story
words.example: The novel's {plot} is its chain of events, from beginning to end.

words.definition: a piece of writing giving an opinion about a book or show
words.example: The {review} is a critic's written opinion piece, awarding the comedy four stars.

words.definition: a television service that shows its own set of programmes
words.example: Tune to this television {channel}, a numbered service broadcasting its own programmes.

words.definition: worried about something that is about to happen
words.example: My hands shake before performances because I feel {nervous} on stage.

words.definition: unhappy because something was worse than you hoped
words.example: I felt {disappointed} that my long-awaited birthday outing was cancelled.

words.definition: uncomfortable because other people have seen you do something silly
words.example: I felt {embarrassed} when everyone noticed my trousers were on backwards.

words.definition: unhappy because someone else has something you want
words.example: I felt {jealous} of my brother because I wanted his new bike.

words.definition: happy because something worrying has ended or did not happen
words.example: I felt {relieved}: my worry disappeared when the lost dog came home.

words.definition: feeling that you want to thank someone for helping you
words.example: I am {grateful} for your help and want to thank you.

words.definition: showing good manners and respect for other people
words.example: Saying please and thank you is {polite} behaviour.

words.definition: telling the truth and not cheating
words.example: An {honest} player admits touching the ball, even when nobody saw.

words.definition: happy to give others more than they expect
words.example: Our {generous} neighbour gives away far more food than anyone expects.

words.definition: the feeling of liking and caring about someone you know well
words.example: Our {friendship} began when we met and started spending time together.

words.definition: sports such as running, jumping and throwing
words.example: The {athletics} competition includes running races, high jump and discus.

words.definition: a sport involving controlled movements, balances and jumps
words.example: In {gymnastics}, we practise cartwheels and balances on a narrow beam.

words.definition: a sport where players hit a feathered object over a net
words.example: In {badminton}, players hit a shuttlecock over a net with rackets.

words.definition: the person or team you are playing against
words.example: My chess {opponent} sits opposite me and moves the black pieces.

words.definition: the person who makes sure players follow the rules
words.example: The {referee} blew the whistle and awarded a free kick.

words.definition: a series of games to find an overall winner
words.example: Eight teams enter this {tournament}, but only one wins the final.

words.definition: a result where both sides finish with the same score
words.example: The match ended in a {draw}, with two goals for each team.

words.definition: a practice of a performance before people come to see it
words.example: At the dress {rehearsal}, actors practise the whole play in costume.

words.definition: clothes worn to look like someone else in a performance
words.example: My stage {costume} includes a crown because I play the king.

words.definition: the raised area where people perform in a theatre
words.example: Actors perform on {stage} in a theatre, facing the audience.

words.definition: a piece of paper showing what you bought and paid
words.example: Keep the shop {receipt} as proof that you paid for these shoes.

words.definition: money given back when you return something you bought
words.example: The shop gave me a full {refund} when I returned the broken toy.

words.definition: an amount taken off the usual price
words.example: A ten-pound {discount} reduced the price from fifty pounds to forty.

words.definition: how big or small something is
words.example: These shoes are too tight; I need a larger {size}.

words.definition: money in the form of coins and notes
words.example: The stall accepts only {cash}, so bring coins or notes.

words.definition: money returned when you pay more than something costs
words.example: The {change} due from my five-pound note is two pounds for a three-pound book.

words.definition: someone buying goods or services from a business
words.example: The shopkeeper helped the {customer} choose a coat to buy.

words.definition: a line of people waiting for their turn
words.example: We joined the {queue} and waited behind five people for tickets.

words.definition: completely new and never used
words.example: Straight from the factory and never previously owned, these trainers are {brand-new}.

words.definition: owned or used by someone else before you
words.example: After two years on another child's feet, these {second-hand} boots became mine.

words.definition: to make something broken work again
words.example: We {repair} broken chairs, fixing their joints instead of buying replacements.

words.definition: to put a new thing in the place of another
words.example: We must {replace} the empty battery with a new one.

words.definition: to put things in their proper places
words.example: Please {tidy} your room by putting every toy back in its box.

words.definition: to put things into a bag or case for travelling
words.example: I {pack} my suitcase by putting clothes inside, ready for our holiday.

words.definition: to take things out of a bag or case
words.example: At the hotel, I {unpack} my suitcase and put clothes in drawers.

words.definition: to stop a machine or light from working using its control
words.example: Please {switch off} the lamp by pressing its power button.

words.definition: to take care of someone or something
words.example: I will {look after} your rabbit by feeding it while you're away.

words.definition: to try to find someone or something
words.example: Can you {look for} my missing keys under the sofa?

words.definition: to board a bus, train or other large vehicle
words.example: To start riding, we {get on} the bus and find empty seats.

words.definition: to leave a bus, train or other large vehicle
words.example: We {get off} the train, stepping from the carriage onto the station platform.
